content:
If you open Apple Maps today, you'll notice that Apple has begun renaming Lake Ontario to "Lake America." This name change follows an executive order from Trump last week, part of his ongoing trade dispute with Canada.

The change, first spotted by Bloomberg, applies to Apple Maps users in the United States. Canadian Apple Maps users will still see the name "Lake Ontario." Apple Maps users in other regions will see both names displayed together.

Google Maps had already renamed Lake Ontario to Lake America earlier. At the time, Google stated that its policy is to use the names designated by the U.S. Geographic Names Information System (GNIS).

U.S. Interior Secretary Doug Burgum said yesterday that Trump has "directly contacted Apple" to request this change. It appears that this conversation prompted Apple to follow suit and update the name on Apple Maps.

Meanwhile, MapQuest announced last Thursday that it refused to rename Lake Ontario to Lake America, a decision that caused its download numbers to surge.

The change appears to be rolling out gradually to Apple Maps users. My own iPhone still shows Lake Ontario, but some of my colleagues at 9to5Mac are already seeing Lake America.

Last year, when Trump ordered the Gulf of Mexico to be renamed "America Gulf," Apple similarly made the change on Apple Maps.
